proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By definition of the floor function, m := floor(x) is an integer such that m <= x < m + 1. Define f := x - m. Then f >= 0 because x >= m, and f < 1 because x < m + 1. By the usual definition of the fractional part, frac(x) = x - floor(x) = x - m = f. Therefore x = m + f = floor(x) + frac(x), and also 0 <= frac(x) < 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Use the defining property of floor: m=floor(x) satisfies m<=x<m+1. Setting f=x-m gives 0<=f<1, and f is exactly frac(x). Hence x=floor(x)+frac(x) with 0<=frac(x)<1 for all real x.
vetter_reason: The proof directly establishes the stated decomposition of an arbitrary real number into its integer part and fractional part, and correctly verifies 0 <= frac(x) < 1. It matches the lemma exactly and uses only standard floor/fractional-part definitions.
